rules.name: is_vocabulary_consistent
rules.instructions: Do the identifiers in this file keep one vocabulary - the same concept always the same word?

criteria.true: The identifiers in this file keep one vocabulary with each other: the same concept always keeps the same word, and the same role keeps the same suffix or verb convention.
criteria.false: Synonym drift is present: the same concept is referred to by two different words within the file (user in one place, account for the same thing in another; cart versus basket), forcing a reader to learn two names for one idea. Different words for genuinely different concepts are not drift.

rules.name: is_naming_convention_consistent
rules.instructions: Do identifiers of the same kind in this file follow a single casing convention?

criteria.true: Identifiers of the same kind follow one casing convention in this file - functions and variables in camelCase, types and classes in PascalCase, module-level constants in SCREAMING_SNAKE - or whichever single form the file has already established for that kind. Different kinds may use different conventions, and a mixed name quality or mixed name shape is not this defect.
criteria.false: Two different casing forms appear for the same kind within the file (getUserData beside fetch_user_data for two functions, OrderItem beside order_item for two types), forcing a reader to learn two shapes for one kind.

rules.name: is_naming_shape_consistent
rules.instructions: Do identifiers that fill the same role in this file follow one morphological pattern - the same way of ordering the action and the object in a name (lead with the action, or lead with the thing it acts on) and the same suffixing style for that role - independent of casing?

criteria.true: Identifiers that fill the same role are built on one morphological pattern: names that state an action all lead with the action (verb-headed) or all lead with the thing acted on (noun-headed), and the same agent-suffix style (-er/-or) is used consistently for that role. The reader never has to re-learn which element of the name is the verb. Casing is not part of this judgment, and word choice or name quality are not shape failures.
criteria.false: Identifiers of the same role mix morphological patterns: some names lead with the action while others lead with the object, or the same role alternates between bare verbs and agent-suffixed forms with no rule - so a reader cannot tell from the name's pattern what role the name plays without checking each one. Different roles may use different patterns; word choice, name quality, and casing are separate judgments.
